title: Do not use `len(SEQUENCE)` without comparison to determine if a sequence is empty.
summary: Empty sequences are considered false in a boolean context. You can either remove the call to 'len' (if not x) or compare the length against a scalar (if len(x) > 1). pylint calls it use-implicit-booleaness-not-len.
message_templates: Do not use `len(SEQUENCE)` without comparison to determine if a sequence is empty

title: "…" can be simplified to "…", if it is strictly a sequence, as an empty … is falsey.
summary: Empty sequences are considered false in a boolean context. Following this check blindly in weakly typed code base can create hard to debug issues. If the value can be something else that is falsey but not a sequence (for example None, an empty string, or 0) the code will not be equivalent. pylint calls it use-implicit-booleaness-not-comparison.
message_templates: "{}" can be simplified to "{}", if it is strictly a sequence, as an empty {} is falsey

title: "…" can be simplified to "…", if it is strictly an int, as 0 is falsey.
summary: 0 is considered false in a boolean context. Following this check blindly in weakly typed code base can create hard to debug issues. If the value can be something else that is falsey but not an int (for example None, an empty string, or an empty sequence) the code will not be equivalent. pylint calls it use-implicit-booleaness-not-comparison-to-zero.
